clue.text: Woman not quite a hottie? That's a bit sexist

indicators.note: not quite means the word for a woman stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: a lady is a woman
a dish is slang for an attractive person, a hottie

explanation.surface: Someone calls a woman nearly a hottie and is told off for a mildly sexist remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish behaviour is boorish and macho, typically including casual sexism, so it is a bit sexist.

clue.text: Uncultured spat after wife's caught in fling

indicators.note: after means the word for spat comes after the first part
caught in means the letter for wife is held within the word for fling

parts.note: to lob is to fling or toss
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
a spat is a quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: A boorish person squabbles once their wife has been caught having an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' looks like an affair but is the verb to throw, LOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowbrow describes tastes that are unsophisticated, the opposite of highbrow culture.

clue.text: Tense about wild fun in baths with little liquid

indicators.note: about here means the word for tense is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: stressed means tense, anxious

indicators.note: in means the scrambled letters sit inside the word for baths

parts.note: the baths is a public swimming pool

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of fun are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An anxious person frets about some wild fun in the swimming baths, with just a little water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns STRESSED back to DESSERTS; 'wild' makes NFU from fun, which goes 'in' POOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon used for pudding holds a small measured quantity of liquid, about two teaspoons' worth.

clue.text: Liberated eroticism in the same form

indicators.note: liberated means the letters are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Liberated eroticism takes the same shape as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberated' rearranges eroticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric means having equal dimensions or measurements, so things drawn that way keep the same proportions.

clue.text: I'm surprised about the main part of scripture

indicators.note: about here means the exclamation is turned back to front

parts.note: oh is an exclamation of surprise
the main is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: Someone expresses surprise at the central portion of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns OH into HO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Hosea is one of the minor prophets in the Old Testament, so a section of the Bible.

clue.text: Really scoffed about performer finishing early

indicators.note: about means the word for scoffed is read in reverse

parts.note: scoffed means fed greedily, ate

indicators.note: finishing early means the performer word loses its final letter

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: Someone truly wolfed food down while thinking about a performer who left early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns FED into DEF; ACTOR loses its last letter to give ACTO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in fact or in reality, as opposed to officially, so it can stand for really.

clue.text: Two characters together swim with hot swimwear

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a thong is a skimpy bathing garment

explanation.surface: A pair of people go for a swim together in revealing hot swimwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two characters' suggests people, but means two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A diphthong is two vowel letters written together as a single sound, as in the ligature ae.

clue.text: Pro with golf ball to accept losing

parts.note: for means in favour of, pro
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O looks like a ball

explanation.surface: A professional golfer with the ball has to resign themselves to defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a golf professional but means in favour, FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to go without it, giving it up willingly.

clue.text: Official blamed over drug-smuggling cases

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first word sits above the rest

parts.note: charged means accused, blamed

indicators.note: smuggling means the drug is carried hidden inside the cases word

parts.note: affairs are matters or cases
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An official is blamed over cases of drug smuggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggling' puts E inside AFFAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat who stands in for an ambassador, or heads a minor mission, holds this title.

clue.text: Finished interminable fight late

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: interminable means without an end, so the fight word loses its last letter

parts.note: a duel is a fight between two people

explanation.surface: A seemingly endless fight is finally over, but too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' drops the last letter of DUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived by the expected time, so it is behind schedule.

clue.text: Town street crossed by setters having great horse-riding experience?

indicators.note: crossed by means the street abbreviation cuts through the rest

parts.note: crossword setters writing together call themselves we
a rider having a great experience is on a super mare, a fine female horse

explanation.surface: A town's street is crossed by setters who enjoy a splendid ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading of the setters on a super mare. Weston-super-Mare is an English seaside resort in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: Weston-super-Mare is a seaside resort on the Bristol Channel coast of Somerset, England.

clue.text: Bird concealed by tree vegetation

indicators.note: concealed by means the answer is tucked away within the words tree vegetation

explanation.surface: A bird is hiding in the foliage of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird of the sandpiper family.

clue.text: Following trail back on rocky coast leads to disasters

indicators.note: in an across clue on means the latter pieces come after the scrambled part
rocky means unsteady, so the letters of coast are shaken into a new order

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: back means the word for trail is read in reverse

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail or follow them

explanation.surface: Following a path back along a rocky shoreline leads to catastrophes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' makes ACTSO from coast; 'back' turns DOG into GOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers use the phrase for natural catastrophes such as floods or earthquakes beyond human control.

clue.text: Women playing pelota, or another game

indicators.note: playing means the letters are messed about with to form a new order

explanation.surface: Women are playing the Basque ball game pelota or some other sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges pelota and or into ATERPOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a team ball sport played in a swimming pool, so it is a game other than pelota.

clue.text: Prayer of 4, heartbroken

indicators.note: broken means the combined letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: the number 4 is spelt out as four

explanation.surface: A prayer is said for the person at 4 Down, whose heart is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a reference to 4 Down but is just the word four; 'broken' rearranges FOUR with heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Prayer is often named by its opening two words in English.

clue.text: Scheme with Italian bigwig fencing diamonds

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the bigwig surrounds the diamonds letter

parts.note: the doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A plot involving an Italian big shot who fences stolen diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' looks like dealing in stolen goods but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick or scam, a scheme for getting round something.

clue.text: Carpet to appear scruffier

definitions.meaning: to carpet someone is to give them a severe telling-off
to wear casual clothes, looking less smart than usual

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to scold someone and to wear clothes that are less formal than usual.

clue.text: Republican's out of line about earth issue

indicators.note: out of means the Republican's letter has left the line word

parts.note: a tropic is a line of latitude running round the earth
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican has strayed from the party line on the subject of the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from TROPIC; the 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a subject or matter under discussion, a theme.

clue.text: Stunned, with seat newly favouring Corbyn?

indicators.note: newly means the letters of seat are made anew in another order

parts.note: Jeremy Corbyn, former UK Labour leader, is on the hard left, so his supporters are red

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that a seat has just gone over to a Corbyn supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges seat into TASE. Corbyn led Britain's Labour Party from 2015 to 2020.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tasered has been hit with an electric stun gun, so they are stunned.

clue.text: Rook with bird flu awfully sorry

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
an egret is a heron-like bird

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of flu are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rook that has given another bird flu feels terribly apologetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges flu to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling regret means being sorry or apologetic about something.

clue.text: Draw seal ultimately, like an aquatic creature?

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so only the last letter of seal is used

parts.note: ottery is a playful made-up adjective meaning like an otter

explanation.surface: A sketch of a seal looks, in the end, rather like some other water animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like an aquatic creature' is a whimsical coinage, otter plus -y, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw in which prizes go to randomly chosen tickets.

clue.text: Pen gripping love novel to reveal nothing

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the pen word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a stall is a pen or enclosure for an animal
love is zero in tennis, written as O
novel means new

explanation.surface: A writer gripped by a love story gives nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' and 'novel' suggest writing; they mean an animal stall and new.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct by refusing to answer or give any information.

clue.text: See limits for one verse

indicators.note: limits means the see word forms the boundaries around the other letters

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
eg, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: Look at the restrictions on a single line of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the bishopric of Ely, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, especially a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Sensationalist cover, in which solver is in text

indicators.note: in which means the other letters are placed within the cover word

parts.note: a lid is a cover
in text-message shorthand, you are is written UR, and the solver is you

explanation.surface: A lurid book jacket that shows the reader inside the text.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver is 'you', so 'solver is' is 'you are', texted as UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid writing is shocking and garish, presented to create a sensation.

clue.text: Must old-fashioned Sierra stop moving?

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to halt is to stop moving

explanation.surface: Does an old Ford Sierra car have to come to a standstill?
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Sierra is an old car model, hinting at the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalt is the archaic second person form of shall, as in thou shalt not, expressing obligation.

clue.text: Help student's received, perhaps

indicators.note: received means taken in, so the student word is held inside the help word

parts.note: recourse is a source of help to turn to
a fresher is a first-year university student

explanation.surface: Assistance a learner has been given, as one example.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means has; 'perhaps' marks the whole clue as one example of such help.
explanation.definitionFit: A short course that updates old skills is a kind of help a learner may be given.

clue.text: Streamline business of French farm producer

parts.note: de is French for of
a layer is a hen that produces eggs on a farm

explanation.surface: Rationalising the business of a French egg farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To delayer a company is to cut out levels of management, making it leaner.

clue.text: Content to leave dirty, horrid old soap

indicators.note: content to leave means the inner letters of dirty depart, keeping only its outside

parts.note: nasty means horrid

explanation.surface: Happy to abandon dirty, horrible old soap rather than wash with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy but means the insides of dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynasty was a glossy American television soap opera of the 1980s.
